name: Uganda
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: Bantu farmers settle the lakes region
claims.summary: Iron-using Bantu-speaking agriculturalists spread into the interlacustrine region north and west of Lake Victoria, establishing the banana-farming societies that underlie the later kingdoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-500bce-bantu-farmers-settle-the-lakes-region, claim TL:UGA:event:500bce:bantu-farmers-settle-the-lakes-region, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of Bunyoro-Kitara
claims.summary: The kingdom of Bunyoro-Kitara, ruled by the omukama and linked in tradition to the Bachwezi, emerges as the dominant power of the interlacustrine region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1000-rise-of-bunyoro-kitara, claim TL:UGA:event:1000:rise-of-bunyoro-kitara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of Buganda
claims.summary: Buganda takes shape east of Bunyoro under its first kabakas; tradition credits its founding to Kintu or, in Bunyoro accounts, to Kato Kimera of the Babito dynasty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1400-foundation-of-buganda, claim TL:UGA:event:1400:foundation-of-buganda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Buganda expands at Bunyoro's expense
claims.summary: Under a line of aggressive kabakas, the compact kingdom of Buganda annexes territory from Bunyoro-Kitara, growing into the largest state in the interlacustrine region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1650-buganda-expands-at-bunyoro-s-expense, claim TL:UGA:event:1650:buganda-expands-at-bunyoro-s-expense, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Swahili-Arab traders reach Buganda
claims.summary: A caravan led by Ahmed bin Ibrahim reaches the court of Kabaka Suna II, opening Buganda to the Zanzibar-based ivory and slave trade and to Islam.

sources.label: Guns and ivory: How Arab traders uncovered the heartbeat of Africa
White Fathers, Islam and Kiswahili in Nineteenth-Century Uganda

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1844-swahili-arab-traders-reach-buganda, claim TL:UGA:event:1844:swahili-arab-traders-reach-buganda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Anglican missionaries arrive
claims.summary: Agents of the Church Missionary Society reach Buganda after Stanley publicises Mutesa I's apparent interest in Christianity, beginning Protestant evangelism at the kabaka's court.

sources.label: White Fathers, Islam and Kiswahili in Nineteenth-Century Uganda

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1877-anglican-missionaries-arrive, claim TL:UGA:event:1877:anglican-missionaries-arrive, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Catholic White Fathers arrive
claims.summary: Roman Catholic missionaries of the White Fathers reach Buganda, adding a third faith to the rivalry of Muslim, Protestant and Catholic factions at court.

sources.label: White Fathers, Islam and Kiswahili in Nineteenth-Century Uganda

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1879-catholic-white-fathers-arrive, claim TL:UGA:event:1879:catholic-white-fathers-arrive, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Martyrdom of Charles Lwanga
claims.summary: Kabaka Mwanga II has Charles Lwanga and a group of Christian pages burned to death at Namugongo, the most notorious episode in the killing of the Uganda Martyrs of 1885–87.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1886-martyrdom-of-charles-lwanga, claim TL:UGA:event:1886:martyrdom-of-charles-lwanga, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Killing of the Uganda Martyrs
claims.summary: Mwanga II executes some forty-five Catholic and Anglican converts who refuse to renounce their faith; twenty-two Catholic victims were later canonised as saints.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1885-killing-of-the-uganda-martyrs, claim TL:UGA:event:1885:killing-of-the-uganda-martyrs, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Uganda Protectorate declared
claims.summary: Britain proclaims a protectorate over Buganda, soon extended across the wider territory, beginning sixty-eight years of colonial rule administered through the kingdoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1894-uganda-protectorate-declared, claim TL:UGA:event:1894:uganda-protectorate-declared, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Uganda Railway is built
claims.summary: The railway is driven from Mombasa to Kisumu on Lake Victoria by some 32,000 indentured Indian labourers, binding Uganda to the coast and bringing a lasting South Asian presence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1896-the-uganda-railway-is-built, claim TL:UGA:event:1896:the-uganda-railway-is-built, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Buganda Agreement
claims.summary: Sir Harry Johnston and Buganda's regents sign the agreement recognising the kabaka and Lukiiko, creating the 'mailo' land system and entrenching Buganda's privileged status under indirect rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1900-the-buganda-agreement, claim TL:UGA:event:1900:the-buganda-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Path to independence negotiated
claims.summary: Constitutional conferences in London settle a federal arrangement preserving Buganda's special status, clearing the way for Ugandan self-government and independence.

sources.label: U.S. Relations With Uganda / History
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1962-path-to-independence-negotiated, claim TL:UGA:event:1962:path-to-independence-negotiated, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Uganda gains independence
claims.summary: Uganda becomes independent from the United Kingdom with Milton Obote as prime minister; the constitution preserves a federal status for Buganda and the other kingdoms.

sources.label: U.S. Relations With Uganda / History
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1962-uganda-gains-independence, claim TL:UGA:event:1962:uganda-gains-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mutesa II becomes first president
claims.summary: Uganda becomes a republic and the kabaka of Buganda, Sir Edward Mutesa II, is elected its first president, a largely ceremonial post under the 1962 constitution.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1963-mutesa-ii-becomes-first-president, claim TL:UGA:event:1963:mutesa-ii-becomes-first-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Mengo and the fall of Buganda
claims.summary: Obote suspends the constitution and orders the army under Idi Amin to storm the kabaka's palace; hundreds die and Mutesa II flees into exile, dying in London in 1969.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1966-battle-of-mengo-and-the-fall-of-buganda, claim TL:UGA:event:1966:battle-of-mengo-and-the-fall-of-buganda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kingdoms abolished
claims.summary: A new republican constitution abolishes the kingdoms of Buganda, Bunyoro, Ankole and Toro and makes Obote executive president of a centralised, unitary Uganda.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1967-kingdoms-abolished, claim TL:UGA:event:1967:kingdoms-abolished, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Amin's coup
claims.summary: While Obote is abroad, army commander Idi Amin overthrows the government in a military coup, beginning eight years of dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1971-amin-s-coup, claim TL:UGA:event:1971:amin-s-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Expulsion of the Asian community
claims.summary: Amin orders the roughly 80,000 South Asians in Uganda to leave within about ninety days, seizing their property and businesses and devastating the economy.

sources.label: Ugandan Asians: 50 years since their expulsion from Uganda

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1972-expulsion-of-the-asian-community, claim TL:UGA:event:1972:expulsion-of-the-asian-community, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mass killings under Amin
claims.summary: Amin's regime murders soldiers, professionals, clergy and dissidents through bodies such as the State Research Bureau; estimates of the dead run up to about 300,000.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1971-mass-killings-under-amin, claim TL:UGA:event:1971:mass-killings-under-amin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Murder of Archbishop Luwum
claims.summary: The Anglican archbishop Janani Luwum, who had protested against state violence, is killed; his death becomes a symbol of the regime's brutality.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1977-murder-of-archbishop-luwum, claim TL:UGA:event:1977:murder-of-archbishop-luwum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Uganda–Tanzania War
claims.summary: After Amin invades northern Tanzania, Julius Nyerere's forces and Ugandan exiles counter-attack and capture Kampala in April 1979, driving Amin into exile.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1978-uganda-tanzania-war, claim TL:UGA:event:1978:uganda-tanzania-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Obote returns to power
claims.summary: After interim governments under Lule and Binaisa, disputed elections return Milton Obote and the UPC to power; opponents allege the vote was rigged.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1980-obote-returns-to-power, claim TL:UGA:event:1980:obote-returns-to-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ugandan Bush War
claims.summary: Museveni's National Resistance Army wages guerrilla war against Obote's government from the Luwero Triangle; the army's counter-insurgency kills and displaces many thousands of civilians.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1981-the-ugandan-bush-war, claim TL:UGA:event:1981:the-ugandan-bush-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Museveni captures Kampala
claims.summary: The National Resistance Army takes Kampala and Yoweri Museveni is sworn in as president, ending the post-Amin upheaval and beginning his long rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1986-museveni-captures-kampala, claim TL:UGA:event:1986:museveni-captures-kampala, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Lord's Resistance Army
claims.summary: Joseph Kony forms the Lord's Resistance Army in northern Uganda, launching an insurgency notorious for atrocities and the abduction of children.

sources.label: Q&A on Joseph Kony and the Lord's Resistance Army

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1987-rise-of-the-lord-s-resistance-army, claim TL:UGA:event:1987:rise-of-the-lord-s-resistance-army, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cultural kingdoms restored
claims.summary: Museveni's government restores the kingdoms in a cultural, non-political form; a new kabaka of Buganda, Ronald Mutebi II, is enthroned.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-1993-cultural-kingdoms-restored, claim TL:UGA:event:1993:cultural-kingdoms-restored, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Term limits removed
claims.summary: Parliament removes presidential term limits from the constitution, and Uganda returns to multiparty politics; Museveni's tenure lengthens into one of Africa's longest.

sources.label: Uganda: Bill Eliminating Presidential Age Limit
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Global Legal Monitor

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-2005-term-limits-removed, claim TL:UGA:event:2005:term-limits-removed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: LRA driven from Uganda
claims.summary: After nearly two decades that displaced almost two million people and saw tens of thousands of children abducted, the Lord's Resistance Army is pushed out of northern Uganda.

sources.label: Q&A on Joseph Kony and the Lord's Resistance Army

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uganda: From the great lakeside kingdoms of the Buganda kabakas to a turbulent modern republic.", terralore.co/country/UGA/chronicle#ev-2006-lra-driven-from-uganda, claim TL:UGA:event:2006:lra-driven-from-uganda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
